records.source: וַנֵּ֣פֶן וַנַּ֔עַל דֶּ֖רֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֑ן וַיֵּצֵ֣א עוֹג֩ מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָׁ֨ן לִקְרָאתֵ֜נוּ ה֧וּא וְכָל־עַמּ֛וֹ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה אֶדְרֶֽעִי׃
records.gloss: And we turned and went up [the] way of the Bashan, and came out Og king of the Bashan to meet us, he and all his people, for the battle [at] Edrei.
pieces: Then we turned and went up along the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us with all his army to do battle at Edrei.

L.1: And we turned and went up [by] the way of Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out to meet us, he and all his people, for battle at Edrei.

R.1: Next we turned north and went up the road toward Bashan. Og, the king of Bashan, came out with his whole army to fight us at Edrei.

decisions.choice: we turned, we went up: Moses goes on telling the journey, speaking for himself and Israel
decisions.reason: The chapter lies inside Moses' first speech (1:6-4:40). He is still recalling the march, which reached the land east of the Jordan in chapter 2. Verses 1-7 retell the victory over Og told in Numbers 21:33-35, in almost the same words.

decisions.choice: Bashan, Og, Edrei: the high country north of Gilead, its king, and a royal town on its southern edge
decisions.reason: Bashan was the fertile tableland east and north-east of the Sea of Galilee, known for its cattle and oaks (32:14; Isaiah 2:13). Og ruled it from Ashtaroth and Edrei (1:4; Joshua 12:4).

decisions.choice: to meet us ... all his people: to confront us in battle with all his fighting men
decisions.reason: "To meet" someone with an army and "for battle" means to march out against them. "His people" here are the men who fought for him, as in Numbers 21:33.

decisions.choice: no opening quotation mark
decisions.reason: Moses' first speech opened its quotation at 1:6 and closes it at 4:40. Records in between carry no outer quotation marks, and words that Moses quotes inside the speech take single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: army; Readable "north"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "army" for "his people" in battle. Readable adds "north", since the road to Bashan led north from the land of Sihon.

records.heading: The defeat of Og king of Bashan

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ אַל־תִּירָ֣א אֹת֔וֹ כִּ֣י בְיָדְךָ֞ נָתַ֧תִּי אֹת֛וֹ וְאֶת־כָּל־עַמּ֖וֹ וְאֶת־אַרְצ֑וֹ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֗יתָ לְסִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to me, do not fear him, for into your hand I have given him and all his people and his land, and you will do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorite[s] who [was] dwelling in Heshbon.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Do not be afraid of him, for I have handed him over to you, together with all his army and his land. Treat him as you treated Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon.'

L.2: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Do not fear him, for into your hand I have given him and all his people and his land; and you shall do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon.'

R.2: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Do not be afraid of him. I have already given him, his whole army and his land into your power. Do the same to him as you did to Sihon, the Amorite king who ruled from Heshbon.'

decisions.choice: I have given: the victory is spoken of as already done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act. God speaks of the outcome as settled before the battle begins, as he did of Sihon (2:24, 31).

decisions.choice: into your hand: into your power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power and control. "Your" is singular: God speaks to Moses as the leader who stands for the whole people.

decisions.choice: dwelling in Heshbon: living there as its ruler
decisions.reason: The verb means to sit or to dwell, and of a king it can mean to sit on the throne, to reign. Heshbon was Sihon's royal city (2:24-36; Numbers 21:26).

decisions.choice: ruled
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ruled", since a king who "dwells" in a city reigns there. Literal keeps "dwelt".

records.source: וַיִּתֵּן֩ יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֜ינוּ בְּיָדֵ֗נוּ גַּ֛ם אֶת־ע֥וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָׁ֖ן וְאֶת־כָּל־עַמּ֑וֹ וַנַּכֵּ֕הוּ עַד־בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר־ל֖וֹ שָׂרִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And gave Yahweh our God into our hand also Og king of the Bashan and all his people, and we struck him until not he left to him [a] survivor.
pieces: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God handed Og king of Bashan and all his army over to us as well, and we struck him down until not one survivor was left to him.

L.3: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God gave into our hand Og king of Bashan also, and all his people, and we struck him down until no survivor was left to him.

R.3: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God let us defeat King Og of Bashan and his whole army too. We fought them until no one was left alive.

decisions.choice: also: Og falls as Sihon had
decisions.reason: "Also" ties this victory to the one over Sihon (2:33). The two kings fall in the same way, and the next verses tell it in the same pattern (2:34-36).

decisions.choice: until he left no survivor: until no one was left
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. It can be read "until one left him no survivor", meaning simply that none of Og's forces were left alive (Numbers 21:35).

decisions.choice: struck: struck down in battle
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike, and in battle to defeat and kill.

decisions.choice: let us defeat
decisions.reason: Readable says what "gave into our hand" means: the LORD gave Israel the victory.

records.source: וַנִּלְכֹּ֤ד אֶת־כָּל־עָרָיו֙ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔וא לֹ֤א הָֽיְתָה֙ קִרְיָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־לָקַ֖חְנוּ מֵֽאִתָּ֑ם שִׁשִּׁ֥ים עִיר֙ כָּל־חֶ֣בֶל אַרְגֹּ֔ב מַמְלֶ֥כֶת ע֖וֹג בַּבָּשָֽׁן׃
records.gloss: And we captured all his cities at the time the that; not there was [a] town which not we took from them: sixty cities, all [the] region of Argob, [the] kingdom of Og in the Bashan.
pieces: At that time we captured all his towns. There was not a single town we failed to take from them: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob, Og's kingdom in Bashan.

L.4: And we captured all his cities at that time; there was not a town that we did not take from them: sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

R.4: At that time we captured every one of his towns. There was not one town we did not take. There were sixty towns in all. They were in the whole area of Argob, which was Og's kingdom in Bashan.

decisions.choice: the region of Argob: a district of Bashan
decisions.reason: The word for "region" first means a cord or measuring line, and so a stretch of land measured off. Argob was a district within Bashan, named again in verses 13-14 and 1 Kings 4:13. Its exact borders are not known.

decisions.choice: not a town that we did not take: every town, without exception
decisions.reason: The double negative makes a strong statement: every one of Og's towns was taken.

decisions.choice: at that time: the time of these events
decisions.reason: The phrase runs through Moses' retelling (verses 8, 12, 18, 21, 23; 2:34) and marks what happened during the march, as he looks back on it.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:2, Literal says "cities" and Balanced and Readable "towns", since these were mostly small walled places.

records.source: כָּל־אֵ֜לֶּה עָרִ֧ים בְּצֻר֛וֹת חוֹמָ֥ה גְבֹהָ֖ה דְּלָתַ֣יִם וּבְרִ֑יחַ לְבַ֛ד מֵעָרֵ֥י הַפְּרָזִ֖י הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: All these [were] cities fortified [with] wall high, [double] doors and bar, apart from [the] cities of the open-country [dwellers], very many.
pieces: Every one of these towns was fortified with high walls and with barred double gates, and there were very many open villages besides.

L.5: All these [were] cities fortified [with] high walls, doors and bars, besides the towns of the open country, very many.

R.5: All these towns had strong defenses, with high walls and gates that could be barred shut. There were also a great many villages without walls.

decisions.choice: doors and bar: gates of two leaves closed with a bar
decisions.reason: The word for "doors" is in the form used for pairs: a city gate had two leaves, and a beam was set across them to lock them (Judges 16:3; 1 Kings 4:13).

decisions.choice: the open country: unwalled settlements
decisions.reason: The word describes people who live in the open, in places without walls (Esther 9:19; Ezekiel 38:11). These are the farming villages around the walled towns.

decisions.choice: besides ... very many: these villages were taken too
decisions.reason: "Apart from" adds the villages to the sixty walled towns: Israel took both.

decisions.choice: barred double gates; open villages
decisions.reason: Balanced says "barred double gates" for the doors and bar of a city gate, and "open villages" for "the towns of the open country"; Readable says "villages without walls".

records.source: וַנַּחֲרֵ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔ינוּ לְסִיחֹ֖ן מֶ֣לֶךְ חֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן הַחֲרֵם֙ כָּל־עִ֣יר מְתִ֔ם הַנָּשִׁ֖ים וְהַטָּֽף׃
records.gloss: And we devoted to destruction them as we did to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting to destruction every city of men, the women and the little ones.
pieces: We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting every town to destruction, men, women and children.

L.6: And we devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting to destruction every city: men, the women and the little ones.

R.6: We destroyed them completely, as given over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, just as we had done to King Sihon of Heshbon. We destroyed every town and its men, women and children.

decisions.choice: devote to destruction: give over to God completely, keeping nothing
decisions.reason: This is the verb for a "devoted thing" (Leviticus 27:28-29): something given over to the LORD for good. In war it means the people of a town are put to death and none are kept as captives, as with Sihon (2:34). The law for the wars in the land is set out in 7:1-5 and 20:16-18.

decisions.choice: devoting to destruction: the verb repeated in its plain form
decisions.reason: The second verb is an infinitive that restates the first, stressing that the act was carried out on every town.

decisions.choice: men: the adult males of each town
decisions.reason: The word is a rare poetic word for men. With "the women and the little ones" it names the whole population of each town, as in 2:34.

decisions.choice: destroyed them completely, as given over to the LORD
decisions.reason: As in Numbers 21:2, Readable gives the sense of "devote to destruction" in plain words. Literal and Balanced keep the term.

records.source: וְכָל־הַבְּהֵמָ֛ה וּשְׁלַ֥ל הֶעָרִ֖ים בַּזּ֥וֹנוּ לָֽנוּ׃
records.gloss: And all the livestock and [the] spoil of the cities we plundered for ourselves.
pieces: The livestock, though, and the goods taken from the towns we kept as plunder for ourselves.

L.7: But all the livestock and the spoil of the cities we took as plunder for ourselves.

R.7: But we kept all the animals and the valuable things from the towns for ourselves.

decisions.choice: livestock and spoil: kept, as with Sihon
decisions.reason: In this war the ban applied to the people, but the animals and goods could be taken as plunder, as in 2:35. In other cases even these were given over to the LORD (Joshua 6:17-19).

decisions.choice: and all the livestock: placed first for contrast
decisions.reason: The objects stand at the head of the sentence, setting what was kept against the people who were destroyed in verse 6.

decisions.choice: the valuable things
decisions.reason: Readable says "valuable things" for the spoil: the goods taken from a captured town.

records.source: וַנִּקַּ֞ח בָּעֵ֤ת הַהִוא֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ מִיַּ֗ד שְׁנֵי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י הָאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן מִנַּ֥חַל אַרְנֹ֖ן עַד־הַ֥ר חֶרְמֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And we took at the time the that the land from [the] hand of [the] two kings of the Amorite[s] who [were] beyond the Jordan, from [the] wadi of Arnon to [the] mountain of Hermon,
pieces: So at that time we took the land of the two Amorite kings across the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon.

L.8: And we took at that time the land from the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who [were] across the Jordan, from the wadi of Arnon to Mount Hermon.

R.8: So at that time we took the land east of the Jordan River from the two Amorite kings. It stretched from the Arnon River in the south to Mount Hermon in the north.

decisions.choice: beyond the Jordan: on the east side of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The phrase is the usual name for the land east of the river, seen from the land west of it (1:1, 5). Moses is speaking on the east side, so here it is a fixed name rather than his own viewpoint. In verses 20 and 25 the same words mean the west side, the land Israel has still to enter.

decisions.choice: from the Arnon to Hermon: the whole land east of the Jordan, south to north
decisions.reason: The Arnon runs west into the Dead Sea and was the southern border of Sihon's land (2:24, 36). Mount Hermon, the high mountain at the north end of the region, was the northern limit of Og's. The word for "wadi" names a stream in a valley and the valley it runs through.

decisions.choice: from the hand of: from the control of
decisions.reason: To take land "from the hand" of a king is to take it out of his power.

decisions.choice: east of the Jordan River; in the south ... in the north
decisions.reason: Readable says where "across the Jordan" lies from Moses' standpoint, and adds the directions so the reader can picture the extent of the land.

records.source: צִידֹנִ֛ים יִקְרְא֥וּ לְחֶרְמ֖וֹן שִׂרְיֹ֑ן וְהָ֣אֱמֹרִ֔י יִקְרְאוּ־ל֖וֹ שְׂנִֽיר׃
records.gloss: Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorite[s] call it Senir.
pieces: (The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.)

L.9: (Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.)

R.9: (The people of Sidon call Mount Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.)

decisions.choice: an aside inside Moses' speech
decisions.reason: The verse breaks off the list of conquered land to explain the other names of Hermon. Such notes stand inside Moses' speech here and in verses 11 and 13-14; the text does not say whether they are Moses' own words or a note added later for readers.

decisions.choice: Sirion, Senir: other peoples' names for Hermon
decisions.reason: The Sidonians were the Phoenicians of the coast to the north-west. "Sirion" is the name in Psalm 29:6, and "Senir" in 1 Chronicles 5:23, Song of Songs 4:8 and Ezekiel 27:5; Senir may sometimes name a peak of the Hermon range.

decisions.choice: parentheses
decisions.reason: The aside is set in parentheses at every level, so that the list of verses 8 and 10 can be read straight through. The outer quotation of Moses' speech stays open.

records.source: כֹּ֣ל׀עָרֵ֣י הַמִּישֹׁ֗ר וְכָל־הַגִּלְעָד֙ וְכָל־הַבָּשָׁ֔ן עַד־סַלְכָ֖ה וְאֶדְרֶ֑עִי עָרֵ֛י מַמְלֶ֥כֶת ע֖וֹג בַּבָּשָֽׁן׃
records.gloss: All [the] cities of the plateau and all the Gilead and all the Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, [the] cities of [the] kingdom of Og in the Bashan.
pieces: We captured every town of the plateau, the whole of Gilead and the whole of Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns that belonged to Og's kingdom in Bashan.

L.10: All the cities of the plateau and all Gilead and all Bashan, as far as Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan.

R.10: We took all the towns on the high plain, all of Gilead, and all of Bashan as far as the towns of Salecah and Edrei. These were towns in Og's kingdom of Bashan.

decisions.choice: all the cities: the list goes on from verse 8
decisions.reason: The verse has no verb of its own. It spells out "the land" that Israel took (verse 8), after the aside of verse 9.

decisions.choice: the plateau, Gilead, Bashan: the three regions east of the Jordan, south to north
decisions.reason: The plateau is the high flat land north of the Arnon, Sihon's land (4:43; Joshua 13:9). Gilead is the hill country on both sides of the Jabbok, and Bashan the land north of it.

decisions.choice: Salecah and Edrei: the edges of Og's land
decisions.reason: Salecah lay at the eastern edge of Bashan (Joshua 13:11; 1 Chronicles 5:11), and Edrei on its south-western side (verse 1).

decisions.choice: We captured / We took
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the verb of verse 8, so the sentence stands on its own after the aside of verse 9.

records.source: כִּ֣י רַק־ע֞וֹג מֶ֣לֶךְ הַבָּשָׁ֗ן נִשְׁאַר֮ מִיֶּ֣תֶר הָרְפָאִים֒ הִנֵּ֤ה עַרְשׂוֹ֙ עֶ֣רֶשׂ בַּרְזֶ֔ל הֲלֹ֣ה הִ֔וא בְּרַבַּ֖ת בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן תֵּ֧שַׁע אַמּ֣וֹת אָרְכָּ֗הּ וְאַרְבַּ֥ע אַמּ֛וֹת רָחְבָּ֖הּ בְּאַמַּת־אִֽישׁ׃
records.gloss: For only Og king of the Bashan was left from [the] remnant of the Rephaim; look, his bed [was a] bed of iron; [is] not it in Rabbah of [the] sons of Ammon? Nine cubits [is] its length and four cubits its width, by [the] cubit of [a] man.
pieces: (Og king of Bashan was the only one left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was made of iron, and it can still be seen in Rabbah of the Ammonites. It is {{units:about 13 1/2 feet long and 6 feet wide|nine cubits long and four cubits wide, by the common cubit}}.)

L.11: (For only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. Look, his bed [was] a bed of iron; [is] it not in Rabbah of the sons of Ammon? Nine cubits [is] its length and four cubits its width, by the cubit of a man.)

R.11: (King Og of Bashan was the last one left of the Rephaim, a people known for their great size. His bed was made of iron, and you can still see it in the Ammonite city of Rabbah. It is {{units:about 13 1/2 feet long and 6 feet wide|nine cubits long and four cubits wide}}.)

decisions.choice: for only Og ...: an aside on Og
decisions.reason: Like verse 9, the verse breaks into the account to explain why Og was remembered. It speaks from a time when the bed was on show in Rabbah, so it may be a note for later readers.

decisions.choice: the remnant of the Rephaim: an ancient people known for their height
decisions.reason: The Rephaim were an old population of the land, remembered as tall and strong (2:10-11, 20-21; Genesis 14:5). Og was the last of them east of the Jordan (Joshua 12:4; 13:12).

decisions.choice: a bed of iron: a bed or couch, made of iron or of dark stone
decisions.reason: The word means a bed or couch (Amos 6:4; Psalm 6:7), and the verse probably describes a great bed of state. Some take it as a coffin, since large stone coffins have been found in the region. "Iron" may also describe the black basalt of Bashan, which looks like iron. Iron was costly at this time, so an iron bed would itself be a mark of power.

decisions.choice: nine cubits by four, by a man's cubit: about 13 1/2 by 6 feet
decisions.reason: "The cubit of a man" is the ordinary cubit, the length of a man's forearm, about 18 inches. The bed was about 13 1/2 feet long and 6 feet wide, far larger than a man needs.

decisions.choice: is it not in Rabbah?: it is there still
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes and points the hearer to something that could be seen. Rabbah was the chief city of the Ammonites (2 Samuel 12:26), where Amman stands today.

decisions.choice: about 13 1/2 feet long and 6 feet wide
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the modern measure, with the cubits as the setting alternative. Literal keeps the cubits.

decisions.choice: it can still be seen / you can still see it; Readable "a people known for their great size"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the question into a plain statement of what it means. Readable says who the Rephaim were, from 2:10-11.

records.source: וְאֶת־הָאָ֧רֶץ הַזֹּ֛את יָרַ֖שְׁנוּ בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑וא מֵעֲרֹעֵ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־עַל־נַ֣חַל אַרְנֹ֗ן וַחֲצִ֤י הַֽר־הַגִּלְעָד֙ וְעָרָ֔יו נָתַ֕תִּי לָרֻֽאוּבֵנִ֖יוְלַגָּדִֽי׃
records.gloss: And the land the this we took possession of at the time the that; from Aroer which [is] by [the] wadi of Arnon, and half [the] hill country of the Gilead and its cities I gave to the Reubenite[s] and to the Gadite[s].
pieces: When we took possession of this land at that time, I gave to the Reubenites and the Gadites the stretch from Aroer beside the Arnon Valley, and half of the hill country of Gilead with its towns.

L.12: And this land we took possession of at that time; from Aroer, which [is] by the wadi of Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead and its cities, I gave to the Reubenites and to the Gadites.

R.12: When we took over this land, I gave part of it to the tribes of Reuben and Gad. Their land started at the town of Aroer by the Arnon River and included half of the hill country of Gilead and its towns.

decisions.choice: Aroer by the Arnon: the southern edge of the land given
decisions.reason: Aroer stood on the northern rim of the Arnon valley, at the southern border of Sihon's land (2:36; Joshua 13:9, 16).

decisions.choice: half the hill country of Gilead: the southern part, up to the Jabbok
decisions.reason: Gilead was divided. Its southern half went to Reuben and Gad (verse 16; Joshua 13:24-25), and the rest to the half-tribe of Manasseh (verse 13).

decisions.choice: I gave: Moses carries out the request of Numbers 32
decisions.reason: Reuben and Gad had asked for this land because it suited their herds, and Moses granted it on condition that their fighting men crossed the Jordan with the other tribes (Numbers 32:1-33; verses 18-20 here).

decisions.choice: When we took possession ..., I gave
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts "this land" first and has two main verbs. Balanced and Readable make the first clause a time clause and set the giving of the land as the main statement.

pieces: To the half-tribe of Manasseh I gave the rest of Gilead and the whole of Bashan, the kingdom of Og. (The whole region of Argob, with all of Bashan, is known as a land of the Rephaim.

L.13: And the rest of Gilead and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh. (All the region of Argob, as to all Bashan, that [land] is called a land of Rephaim.

R.13: I gave the rest of Gilead and all of Bashan, which had been Og's kingdom, to half of the tribe of Manasseh. (The whole area of Argob, all of Bashan, is known as the land of the Rephaim.

decisions.choice: all the region of Argob ...: the start of an aside that runs through verse 14
decisions.reason: The main accent of the verse falls after "Manasseh". What follows explains the region's old name and how Jair took it, a note like those in verses 9 and 11, which ends with "to this day" in verse 14.

decisions.choice: as to all Bashan, that is called: all that part of Bashan is called
alternatives: the whole region of Argob, belonging to all Bashan
decisions.reason: The phrase "as to all Bashan" can mean that Argob belonged to Bashan or that it stands for the whole of it. "That" can point to Bashan ("all that Bashan") or begin a new clause ("it is called"). Either way the land of Argob is the land of the Rephaim.

decisions.choice: the half-tribe of Manasseh: the families of Manasseh settled east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Part of the tribe of Manasseh, the clans of Machir and Jair, took land east of the Jordan (Numbers 32:33, 39-42); the rest of the tribe settled west of it (Joshua 17:1-6).

decisions.choice: land of Rephaim: once held by the Rephaim
decisions.reason: As verse 11 says, Og was the last of the Rephaim, so his land kept their name (2:20).

decisions.choice: parenthesis opening here and closing at the end of verse 14
decisions.reason: As in verses 9 and 11, the aside is set in parentheses. It begins in this verse and ends in the next. Balanced puts "to the half-tribe of Manasseh" first, so that the aside can follow straight after the end of the main sentence.

pieces: Jair, of the line of Manasseh, took all the region of Argob up to the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and he gave these places in Bashan his own name, Havvoth-jair, which they still bear today.)

L.14: Jair son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and he called them, Bashan, by his own name, Havvoth-jair, to this day.)

R.14: Jair, from the tribe of Manasseh, captured the whole area of Argob, up to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites. He named these towns of Bashan after himself. They are still called Havvoth-jair, which means the villages of Jair.)

decisions.choice: Jair son of Manasseh: a descendant of Manasseh
decisions.reason: "Son" here means descendant. Jair belonged to the line of Manasseh (Numbers 32:41; 1 Chronicles 2:21-22).

decisions.choice: Havvoth-jair: "the villages of Jair"
decisions.reason: The first part of the name means tent villages or settlements. The same name is given to Jair's towns in Numbers 32:41 and Judges 10:4.

decisions.choice: the Geshurites and the Maacathites: small kingdoms on the edge of Bashan
decisions.reason: Geshur and Maacah lay north and west of Bashan, toward Mount Hermon, and were not driven out (Joshua 12:5; 13:13). David later married a princess of Geshur (2 Samuel 3:3).

decisions.choice: called them, Bashan ...: named the places of Bashan; "to this day" looks back from a later time
decisions.reason: "Them" refers to the towns of the region, and "the Bashan" stands beside it to say where they were. "To this day" shows that the note speaks from a time when the name was long in use.

decisions.choice: of the line of Manasseh; these places in Bashan / these towns of Bashan; Readable "which means the villages of Jair"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that "son" means descendant, and say what "them" refers to. Readable gives the meaning of the name.

decisions.reason: Machir was the son of Manasseh and the father of the clan that settled in Gilead (Numbers 26:29; 32:39-40). Since the southern half of Gilead went to Reuben and Gad (verses 12, 16), "Gilead" here is the northern part, "the rest of Gilead" of verse 13.

decisions.choice: the family of Machir
decisions.reason: Readable says "the family of", since the land went to Machir's descendants.

pieces: To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the land that runs from Gilead to the Arnon Valley, its boundary running down the center of the valley, and on to the Jabbok River, the boundary of the Ammonites,

L.16: And to the Reubenites and to the Gadites I gave from Gilead as far as the wadi of Arnon, the middle of the wadi and [its] border, and as far as the Jabbok, the wadi, the border of the sons of Ammon,

R.16: I gave the tribes of Reuben and Gad the land from Gilead down to the Arnon River. The middle of the river valley was their southern border. Their land reached as far as the Jabbok River, which was the border of the Ammonites.

decisions.choice: the middle of the wadi and border: the middle of the valley as the border
decisions.reason: "And border" says that the line ran along the middle of the Arnon valley. The same wording is used in Joshua 13:9, 16.

decisions.choice: the Jabbok, the border of the Ammonites: the upper Jabbok on the east
decisions.reason: The upper Jabbok runs north past Rabbah before turning west to the Jordan, and that stretch marked the edge of Ammon's land (Numbers 21:24; Joshua 12:2).

decisions.choice: from Gilead: from the part of Gilead given to them
decisions.reason: The land runs south from Gilead, meaning the half of Gilead in verse 12, to the Arnon.

decisions.choice: their southern border
decisions.reason: Readable adds "southern", since the Arnon was the south edge of their land (verse 12).

L.17: and the Arabah, with the Jordan as [its] border, from Chinnereth as far as the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah toward the east.

R.17: Their land also included the Jordan Valley east of the river, from Lake Chinnereth, which is the Sea of Galilee, down to the Dead Sea, below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.

decisions.choice: the Arabah with the Jordan as border: the eastern side of the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the deep valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea. The part given to the eastern tribes ran along the river, which formed their western border (Joshua 13:27).

decisions.choice: Chinnereth, the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea: the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Chinnereth is the lake later called the Sea of Galilee (Numbers 34:11; Joshua 12:3). The sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, is the Dead Sea (Genesis 14:3; Joshua 3:16).

decisions.choice: the slopes of Pisgah: the hillsides above the north-east end of the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Pisgah is the ridge from which Moses will look over the land (verse 27). Its slopes run down to the shore on the east side.

decisions.choice: the Jordan Valley; Lake Chinnereth, which is the Sea of Galilee; the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Readable uses the names a reader is likely to know, and says that the land lay east of the river.

records.gloss: And I commanded you at the time the that, saying, Yahweh your God has given to you the land the this to possess it; armed you will cross over before your brothers, [the] sons of Israel, all [the] sons of strength.
pieces: At that time I gave you this command: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you this land to possess. But every fighting man among you is to cross over armed, going ahead of your fellow Israelites.

L.18: And I commanded you at that time, saying, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you this land to take possession of it. Armed, you shall cross over before your brothers, the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, all [the] sons of strength.

R.18: At that time I gave an order to the tribes of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh. I said, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} your God has given you this land to be your own. But all your soldiers must take their weapons and cross the river ahead of your fellow Israelites.

decisions.choice: you: the tribes east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: "You" is plural and means Reuben, Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh, to whom the land had just been given (verses 12-13). Moses retells the agreement of Numbers 32:20-32.

decisions.choice: armed: equipped and ready for battle
decisions.reason: The word describes men stripped for action and armed for war (Numbers 32:21, 29; Joshua 4:13).

decisions.choice: all the sons of strength: all the fighting men
decisions.reason: A "son of strength" is a capable, able-bodied man fit for war. The phrase says who must cross: not everyone, but every man able to fight.

decisions.choice: your brothers, the sons of Israel: the other tribes
decisions.reason: "Brothers" is a word for kinsmen. Here it names the rest of Israel, the tribes still to receive land west of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: every fighting man among you / all your soldiers; your fellow Israelites
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable move "all the sons of strength" to the front of the command, which shows who must go. "Your fellow Israelites" gives "your brothers, the sons of Israel" in one phrase. Literal keeps "brothers".

decisions.choice: the tribes of Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh; cross the river
decisions.reason: Readable names the people Moses addressed and says what was to be crossed.

records.gloss: Only your wives and your little ones and your livestock — I know that much livestock [is] to you — will remain in your cities which I have given to you,
pieces: Only your wives and children and your livestock — and I know how much livestock you have — are to stay behind in the towns I have given you,

L.19: Only your wives and your little ones and your livestock — I know that you have much livestock — shall remain in your cities which I have given you,

R.19: Only your wives, your children and your animals may stay in the towns I have given you. I know you have a lot of animals.

decisions.choice: I know that you have much livestock: the reason they asked for this land
decisions.reason: Reuben and Gad wanted the land east of the Jordan because it was good for their herds (Numbers 32:1-5, 16, 26).

decisions.choice: little ones: the children, the dependents of the household
decisions.reason: The word covers children and others too young to fight or travel on their own, as in verse 6.

decisions.choice: which I have given you: Moses speaks of the grant he made
decisions.reason: Moses gave the land as God's leader (verse 12); in verse 18 it is God who has given it.

decisions.choice: I know you have a lot of animals
decisions.reason: Readable moves Moses' remark out of the middle of the sentence and puts it last.

pieces: until {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} grants your fellow Israelites rest, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has granted it to you, and they in turn take possession of the land {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving them across the Jordan. Only then may each of you go back to the holding I have given you.'

L.20: until {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives rest to your brothers as to you, and they also take possession of the land that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving them across the Jordan; then you shall return, each one to his possession which I have given you.'

R.20: Stay with them until {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gives them rest, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given you rest. Wait until they also take over the land west of the Jordan that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God is giving them. After that, each of you may go back to the land I have given you.'

decisions.choice: gives rest: gives a settled, secure life in the land, free from enemies
decisions.reason: Rest is God's promised gift once the land is won (12:9-10; 25:19). Joshua 22:4 tells how the eastern tribes were sent home when it came.

decisions.choice: beyond the Jordan: here the land west of the river
decisions.reason: Moses speaks on the east side, so "beyond the Jordan" here means the land of Canaan that the other tribes are still to enter, unlike verse 8.

decisions.choice: his possession: the land each one holds as his own
decisions.reason: The word means what is taken and held as one's property, the family's share of land.

decisions.choice: as he has granted it to you / as he has given you rest
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "as to you" means: the eastern tribes had already been given rest.

decisions.choice: Stay with them ... Wait until ...; west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Readable breaks the long sentence and supplies the verbs that link it to verse 18. It also says on which side of the river the land lies.

records.gloss: And Joshua I commanded at the time the that, saying, your eyes [are] the [ones] seeing all that did Yahweh your God to [the] two the kings the these; so will do Yahweh to all the kingdoms which you [are] crossing there.
pieces: At that time I commanded Joshua: 'Your own eyes have seen everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did to these two kings. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will deal in the same way with every kingdom you are crossing over to.

L.21: And Joshua I commanded at that time, saying, 'Your eyes [are] the ones that have seen all that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God has done to these two kings; so {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will do to all the kingdoms into which you are crossing.

R.21: At that time I gave Joshua orders. I told him, 'You saw for yourself what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God did to these two kings. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will do that to every kingdom on the other side of the river, where you are going.

decisions.choice: your eyes, you: Joshua; your God: the people
decisions.reason: "Your eyes" and "you are crossing" are singular and speak to Joshua. "Your God" here and "you" in verse 22 are plural, so Joshua is addressed as the leader who stands for the people he will lead.

decisions.choice: and Joshua I commanded: Joshua named first
decisions.reason: Joshua's name stands at the head of the sentence. After the order to the eastern tribes (verse 18), Moses turns to the man who will lead the crossing (1:38; 31:7-8; Numbers 27:18-23).

decisions.choice: the ones seeing: Joshua is an eyewitness
decisions.reason: The participle with the article stresses that Joshua's own eyes saw the victories, and so he has reason to trust what is promised next.

decisions.choice: You saw for yourself
decisions.reason: Readable makes Joshua the subject. Literal and Balanced keep "your eyes" as the subject, which puts the stress on what Joshua himself saw.

decisions.choice: you shall not fear: a firm command, plural

decisions.reason: Balanced gives the stress of the Hebrew "he" with "himself". Readable gives it by making the LORD the one who does the fighting.

pieces: '{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have only begun to show {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} greatness and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong hand. Is there any god in heaven or on earth who can match {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mighty deeds?

L.24: '{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have begun to show {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slave {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} greatness and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} strong hand; for what god [is there] in heaven or on earth who can do according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} works and according to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mighty deeds?

R.24: '{{divine_name:Lord GOD|Lord Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have begun to show me, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, how great and powerful {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are. No god in heaven or on earth can do the great and mighty things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do.

decisions.choice: Lord Yahweh: the title "Lord" joined to God's name
decisions.reason: Moses addresses God as his master and by his name. The same address opens other humble prayers (9:26; Genesis 15:2, 8).

decisions.choice: you have begun: what Moses has seen is only the start
decisions.reason: The victories over Sihon and Og are the first of God's great acts in the conquest. Moses asks to see the rest (verse 25).

decisions.choice: your strong hand: your power at work
decisions.reason: The "strong hand" is God's power shown in deliverance and in war, as at the exodus (Exodus 3:19; Deuteronomy 4:34).

decisions.choice: what god ...?: no god can do such things
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "none". It praises the LORD as beyond comparison. "God" here is the general word for any god (Exodus 15:11).

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slave" for the word Moses uses of himself, and Balanced and Readable say "servant", as the style guide sets out. Calling oneself the master's servant is the humble form of speech used in a request.

decisions.choice: No god ... can do
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a plain statement of what it means.

records.source: אֶעְבְּרָה־נָּ֗א וְאֶרְאֶה֙ אֶת־הָאָ֣רֶץ הַטּוֹבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן הָהָ֥ר הַטּ֛וֹב הַזֶּ֖ה וְהַלְּבָנֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: Let me cross over, please, and let me see the land the good which [is] beyond the Jordan, the hill country the good the this and the Lebanon.
pieces: Please let me go across and see the good land on the far side of the Jordan, this good hill country and the Lebanon.'

L.25: Let me cross over, please, and see the good land that [is] across the Jordan, this good hill country and the Lebanon.'

R.25: Please let me cross the river and see the good land on the other side of the Jordan, with its beautiful hills and the mountains of Lebanon.'

decisions.choice: let me cross over, please: a humble request
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form for a wish, softened with "please". Moses asks as a favor (verse 23), knowing God had already said he would not enter (1:37).

decisions.choice: the good hill country and the Lebanon: the heart of the land and its northern mountains
decisions.reason: The hill country is the central highland of Canaan. Lebanon is the mountain range to the north, named as the northern limit of the land in 1:7 and 11:24.

decisions.choice: beyond the Jordan: the land west of the river, as in verse 20
decisions.reason: Moses stands east of the Jordan, so the land he longs to see is on the far side.

decisions.choice: the mountains of Lebanon; its beautiful hills
decisions.reason: Readable explains that Lebanon is a mountain range and calls the hill country beautiful hills, the sense of "good" here.

records.source: וַיִּתְעַבֵּ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה בִּי֙ לְמַ֣עַנְכֶ֔ם וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֖ע אֵלָ֑י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ רַב־לָ֔ךְ אַל־תּ֗וֹסֶף דַּבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֛י ע֖וֹד בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And was angry Yahweh with me on account of you, and not he listened to me; and said Yahweh to me, enough for you; do not continue to speak to me again in the matter the this.
pieces: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with me because of you and would not listen to me. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Let that be enough! Do not bring this matter up with {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} again.

L.26: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with me on account of you, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not listen to me; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Enough for you! Do not speak to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} again about this matter.

R.26: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was angry with me because of you people, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not listen. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, 'Enough! Do not talk to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} about this anymore.

decisions.choice: was angry: a play on "cross over"
decisions.reason: The verb for "was angry" is a form of the verb "cross over" in verse 25. Moses asked to cross over; instead the LORD's anger "crossed over" against him.

decisions.choice: on account of you: the people's part in Moses' exclusion
decisions.reason: Moses says the same in 1:37 and 4:21. Numbers 20:12 gives Moses' own failure at Meribah as the reason. The two belong together: the people's rebellion led to the event in which Moses failed.

decisions.choice: enough for you: stop, you have said enough
decisions.reason: The same phrase ends a matter in 1:6 and 2:3. Here it closes Moses' request for good.

decisions.choice: Let that be enough! / Enough!
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "enough for you" as English says it. Literal keeps "for you".

records.source: עֲלֵ֣ה׀רֹ֣אשׁ הַפִּסְגָּ֗ה וְשָׂ֥א עֵינֶ֛יךָ יָ֧מָּה וְצָפֹ֛נָה וְתֵימָ֥נָה וּמִזְרָ֖חָה וּרְאֵ֣ה בְעֵינֶ֑יךָ כִּי־לֹ֥א תַעֲבֹ֖ר אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֥ן הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Go up [to the] top of the Pisgah, and lift up your eyes westward and northward and southward and eastward, and see with your eyes, for not you will cross the Jordan the this.
pieces: Climb to the summit of Pisgah and look out to the west, the north, the south and the east. See the land with your own eyes, because you will not cross this Jordan.

L.27: Go up [to the] top of Pisgah and lift up your eyes westward and northward and southward and eastward, and see with your eyes, for you shall not cross this Jordan.

R.27: Go up Mount Pisgah to the very top. Look in every direction: west, north, south and east. Take a good look at the land, because you will not cross the Jordan River.

decisions.choice: lift up your eyes ... in every direction: as Abram was told
decisions.reason: God told Abram to lift up his eyes and look north, south, east and west at the land he would be given (Genesis 13:14-15). Moses is shown the same promised land. Chapter 34:1-4 tells how he did so before he died.

decisions.choice: the top of Pisgah: the ridge above the Jordan valley
decisions.reason: Pisgah is the edge of the high plateau east of the north end of the Dead Sea, with a wide view of the land west of the Jordan (verse 17; Numbers 21:20).

decisions.choice: westward: literally "seaward"
decisions.reason: Hebrew names the west after the sea, the Mediterranean, which lies to the west of the land.

decisions.choice: See the land / Take a good look at the land
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "the land", which is what Moses is to see.

records.source: וְצַ֥ו אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ וְחַזְּקֵ֣הוּ וְאַמְּצֵ֑הוּ כִּי־ה֣וּא יַעֲבֹ֗ר לִפְנֵי֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהוּא֙ יַנְחִ֣יל אוֹתָ֔ם אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And command Joshua and strengthen him and make him strong, for he will cross over before the people the this, and he will cause them to inherit the land which you will see.
pieces: Instead, commission Joshua. Encourage him and give him strength, for he will cross over at the head of this people, and he will give them as their inheritance the land that you will see.'

L.28: And charge Joshua, and strengthen him and make him bold, for he will cross over before this people, and he will cause them to inherit the land that you will see.'

R.28: Give Joshua his orders instead. Encourage him and make him strong. He will lead these people across the river, and he will give them the land that you are about to see, to be their own.'

decisions.choice: charge: appoint to a task with authority
decisions.reason: The verb means to command, and with a person as object to commission him for a work (Numbers 27:19, 23; Deuteronomy 31:7-8, 23).

decisions.choice: strengthen him and make him bold: give him courage
decisions.reason: The pair of verbs is the charge "be strong and courageous" that Joshua will hear again and again (31:7, 23; Joshua 1:6-9).

decisions.choice: cause them to inherit: lead them into the land and share it out
decisions.reason: The verb means to make others inherit. Joshua will bring Israel into the land and divide it among the tribes (1:38; Joshua 13-21).

decisions.choice: Instead
decisions.reason: The "and" sets Joshua's task against Moses' request. Balanced and Readable make that contrast plain.

records.gloss: And we remained in [the] valley opposite Beth-peor.
pieces: So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor.

L.29: And we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor.

R.29: So we stayed in the valley across from Beth-peor.

decisions.choice: Beth-peor: "house of Peor", a place linked with the worship of Baal of Peor
decisions.reason: Near here Israel had joined in the worship of the Baal of Peor (Numbers 25:1-9; Deuteronomy 4:3). This is where Moses gives his speeches (4:46), and he was buried in the valley opposite it (34:6).
